ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A horizontally placed cylinder has an opening at its left end, and the length of the inner wall of the cylinder is $2L$. A piston can only move inside the cylinder, and the right side of the piston is sealed with a certain mass of ideal gas. The thickness of the piston and all friction are negligible, and both the piston and the cylinder are adiabatic. Initially, the piston is at a distance of $L$ from the right end of the cylinder, the external atmospheric pressure is $1.0 \times 10^{5} \mathrm{Pa}$, and the temperature is $27^{\circ}\mathbf{C}$. The sealed gas is now slowly heated using an electric heating wire.

1. What is the distance of the piston from the right end of the cylinder when heated to $227^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$?
2. What is the pressure of the enclosed gas in the cylinder when heated to $527^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a horizontally placed cylinder, with the left end communicating with the outside and the right end closed. There is a very thin vertical piston inside the cylinder, and gas is sealed on the right side of the piston; the figure marks the distance from the piston to the right end as L. The problem statement gives that the total length of the inner wall of the cylinder is 2L, so the piston can move left at most to the left end, at which time the maximum gas length is 2L. Reasoning: Let the cross-sectional area of the cylinder be A. In the initial state, the distance from the piston to the right end is L, so the initial gas volume V0 = AL. The initial temperature T0 = 27℃ = 300 K, and the external atmospheric pressure p0 = 1.0×10^5 Pa. When the piston is frictionless and moves slowly, the gas pressure is balanced with the external atmospheric pressure, namely p = p0; therefore, before the piston reaches the left end, the gas undergoes isobaric expansion, and the volume is directly proportional to the thermodynamic temperature. 1. When heated to 227℃, T1 = 500 K. At this time the gas length x1 satisfies x1/L = T1/T0 = 500/300 = 5/3, so x1 = 5L/3. Because 5L/3 < 2L, the piston has not yet reached the left end, so the result is valid. 2. When heated to 527℃, T2 = 800 K. If it still expanded isobarically, the gas length should be L×800/300 = 8L/3, but 8L/3 > 2L, exceeding the maximum length of the inner wall of the cylinder, so the piston has already reached the left end, and the gas volume is fixed at V = 2AL = 2V0. From the ideal gas state equation pV/T = constant, there is p2 = p0 × (T2/T0) × (V0/V) = 1.0×10^5 × (800/300) × (1/2) = 1.33×10^5 Pa.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a horizontal cylinder open on the left, with a thin piston initially located midway so that the gas on the right occupies a length L, while the whole internal length is 2L; therefore the maximum possible gas length before the piston reaches the left end is 2L. From the text take p0=1.0e5 Pa, T0=27°C=300 K, and requested temperatures 227°C=500 K and 527°C=800 K. While the piston can move freely and slowly, force balance with the open atmosphere gives p=p_atm, so the ideal gas expands isobarically and its length/volume is proportional to absolute temperature. At 500 K, x=L*(500/300)=5L/3, which is below the 2L limit. For 800 K, the unconstrained isobaric length would be L*(800/300)=8L/3>2L, so the piston has already reached the left end; then the volume is fixed at 2 times the initial volume and p=p0*(T/T0)/(V/V0)=1.0e5*(800/300)/2=1.33e5 Pa.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中是一个水平放置的圆筒，左端与外界相通，右端封闭。圆筒内有一个很薄的竖直活塞，活塞右侧封有气体；图中标出活塞到右端的距离为 L。题干给出圆筒内壁总长为 2L，因此活塞向左最多移动到左端，此时气体长度最大为 2L。

推理：设圆筒横截面积为 A。初态活塞到右端距离为 L，所以初态气体体积 V0 = AL。初态温度 T0 = 27℃ = 300 K，外界大气压 p0 = 1.0×10^5 Pa。活塞无摩擦且缓慢移动时，气体压强与外界大气压平衡，即 p = p0，因此在活塞未到达左端前，气体作等压膨胀，体积与热力学温度成正比。

1. 加热到 227℃ 时，T1 = 500 K。此时气体长度 x1 满足 x1/L = T1/T0 = 500/300 = 5/3，所以 x1 = 5L/3。因为 5L/3 < 2L，活塞尚未到达左端，因此结果有效。

2. 加热到 527℃ 时，T2 = 800 K。若仍等压膨胀，气体长度应为 L×800/300 = 8L/3，但 8L/3 > 2L，超过圆筒内壁最大长度，所以活塞已经到达左端，气体体积固定为 V = 2AL = 2V0。由理想气体状态方程 pV/T = 常量，有 p2 = p0 × (T2/T0) × (V0/V) = 1.0×10^5 × (800/300) × (1/2) = 1.33×10^5 Pa。

1. 活塞到右端的距离为 5L/3。
2. 气体压强为 1.33×10^5 Pa。

method.method_draft: Construct the thermodynamic path before calculating. From the drawing, identify that the right-hand gas column initially has length L and can grow only until the piston reaches the open left end, giving a maximum length 2L. From the text, convert temperatures to Kelvin: 300 K initially, 500 K and 800 K finally. Determine the transition temperature first: during the free-piston stage p is constant at atmospheric pressure, so V/T is constant; the gas volume doubles when T doubles, hence the piston reaches the left end at T=600 K. Since 500 K is below 600 K, the gas is still in the constant-pressure stage and the distance from the right end is L*(500/300)=5L/3. Since 800 K is above 600 K, split the process: at 600 K the volume is 2V0 and p=p0; from 600 K to 800 K the piston is stopped and volume is constant, so p/T is constant, giving p=p0*(800/600)=1.33e5 Pa.

推理：初始温度 27°C = 300 K，外界大气压 p0 = 1.0×10^5 Pa。活塞无摩擦且缓慢移动，在未碰到左端前，封闭气体压强始终等于外界大气压，因此经历等压膨胀，V/T 保持不变。气体长度从 L 增大到最大 2L 时，体积加倍，所以温度也应加倍：T = 600 K，此时活塞刚到左端。

1. 加热到 227°C = 500 K，小于 600 K，活塞还未到左端，仍为等压过程。气体长度 x 满足 x/L = 500/300，因此 x = 5L/3。

2. 加热到 527°C = 800 K，大于 600 K。先在 600 K 时达到最大体积 2V0，压强仍为 p0；之后活塞被左端限制，体积不变，故 p/T 保持不变。于是 p = p0 × 800/600 = 1.0×10^5 × 4/3 Pa ≈ 1.33×10^5 Pa。

1. 加热到 227°C = 500 K，小于 600 K，活塞还未到左端，仍为等压过程。气体长度 x 满足 x/L = 500/300，因此 x = 5L/3。

2. 加热到 527°C = 800 K，大于 600 K。先在 600 K 时达到最大体积 2V0，压强仍为 p0；之后活塞被左端限制，体积不变，故 p/T 保持不变。于是 p = p0 × 800/600 = 1.0×10^5 × 4/3 Pa ≈ 1.33×10^5 Pa。
solver_metadata.model_answer:
1. 活塞距右端的距离为 5L/3。
2. 封闭气体压强为 1.33×10^5 Pa。

raw_record.original_question:
A horizontally placed cylinder has an opening at its left end, and the length of the inner wall of the cylinder is $2L$. A piston can only move inside the cylinder, and the right side of the piston is sealed with a certain mass of ideal gas. The thickness of the piston and all friction are negligible, and both the piston and the cylinder are adiabatic. Initially, the piston is at a distance of $L$ from the right end of the cylinder, the external atmospheric pressure is $1.0 \times 10^{5} \mathrm{Pa}$, and the temperature is $27^{\circ}\mathbf{C}$. The sealed gas is now slowly heated using an electric heating wire.

1. What is the distance of the piston from the right end of the cylinder when heated to $227^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$?
2. What is the pressure of the enclosed gas in the cylinder when heated to $527^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$?
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: The figure shows a horizontally placed cylinder, with the left end communicating with the outside and the right end closed. There is a very thin vertical piston inside the cylinder, and gas is sealed on the right side of the piston; the figure marks the distance from the piston to the right end as L. The problem statement gives that the total length of the inner wall of the cylinder is 2L, so the piston can move left at most to the left end, at which time the maximum gas length is 2L.

Reasoning: Let the cross-sectional area of the cylinder be A. In the initial state, the distance from the piston to the right end is L, so the initial gas volume V0 = AL. The initial temperature T0 = 27℃ = 300 K, and the external atmospheric pressure p0 = 1.0×10^5 Pa. When the piston is frictionless and moves slowly, the gas pressure is balanced with the external atmospheric pressure, namely p = p0; therefore, before the piston reaches the left end, the gas undergoes isobaric expansion, and the volume is directly proportional to the thermodynamic temperature.

1. When heated to 227℃, T1 = 500 K. At this time the gas length x1 satisfies x1/L = T1/T0 = 500/300 = 5/3, so x1 = 5L/3. Because 5L/3 < 2L, the piston has not yet reached the left end, so the result is valid.

2. When heated to 527℃, T2 = 800 K. If it still expanded isobarically, the gas length should be L×800/300 = 8L/3, but 8L/3 > 2L, exceeding the maximum length of the inner wall of the cylinder, so the piston has already reached the left end, and the gas volume is fixed at V = 2AL = 2V0. From the ideal gas state equation pV/T = constant, there is p2 = p0 × (T2/T0) × (V0/V) = 1.0×10^5 × (800/300) × (1/2) = 1.33×10^5 Pa.
